chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 540: Li Huowang's Brutal Escape & A New Hallucination
chapter_meta_description: Trapped by the Dharma Sect's endless ranks, Li Huowang escapes using Peng Longteng as a human slingshot—only to face Jin Shan Zhao's plea for help and a new, grotesque hallucination.
og_title: Entrapment – A Dharmic Escape and a Silent Plea
og_description: Li Huowang's bone-sucking burrow attack, a slingshot toss over a sea of cultists, and the cold realization that he is too broken to save anyone.
twitter_title: Ch540: Escaping the Earth, Facing the Dead Mother
twitter_description: Li Huowang wins a tactical escape from the Dharma Sect, but gains a new hallucination: a gaunt woman holding a half-rotted infant.

lore_anchors.definition: A supernatural ability to move through or attack from beneath the earth; in this chapter, it carries a hidden organ-extraction strike.

A powerful, widespread cult in the Dao-Twisted World whose spells and attacks are tied to rock and earth; it is shown to have extremely effective mass-conversion capabilities, even absorbing former Zuowandao members.

A core Daoist internal alchemy term for the original, pre-differentiated vital energy of the universe; here, it is an uncontrollable force within the Heart-Element that can warp reality or self-destruct.
The Mother of the Big Dipper, a high Daoist deity; former Zuowandao members in this novel may have worshipped her before converting to the Dharma Sect.

cultural_notes_faq.a: A half-crippled man who follows Li Huowang after the earthquake incident; he finally speaks his first word ("Help") in this chapter, pleading for the Dharma Sect's cannon-fodder followers.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why can't Li Huowang escape to Great Liang using the spine sword?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Zhuge Yuan warns that if the Dharma Sect has any diviners, they would track the sword's power and make Li Huowang a permanent hunted target in Great Qi.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Who is the new hallucination at the end?
cultural_notes_faq.a: A gaunt, emaciated woman in a white headwrap, holding a half-rotted infant; her identity and origin are unexplained in this chapter.
In Daoist internal alchemy, the pre-differentiated, fundamental vital energy of the universe. In Li Huowang, it is volatile and can cause reality-warping or self-destructive episodes if overused.
